t: An inland Javanese sultanate founded by Panembahan Senapati around 1587, built on the rice lands of Central Java.
Sultan Agung conquered the coastal states, Madura and Surabaya, but twice failed to take Dutch Batavia, in 1628 and 1629.
Rebellion and succession wars made it dependent on the Dutch, and the Treaty of Giyanti split it in two in 1755.
dyk: Sultan Agung’s Javanese calendar of 1633 kept the old Saka year count but switched to Islamic lunar months; it is still used for court ceremonies in Java.
ev: Panembahan Senapati rules Mataram from Kotagede, throwing off Pajang’s authority
Surabaya surrenders to Sultan Agung after a long siege
First of two failed Mataram sieges of Dutch Batavia
Sultan Agung introduces the Javanese calendar
Trunajaya’s rebels sack the capital Plered
Rebels sack Kartasura during the Chinese War
The Treaty of Giyanti divides Mataram into Surakarta and Yogyakarta

f.capital: Kotagede; later Kerta, Plered, Kartasura and Surakarta
